expectations.text: Preserves 18 nurses, four weeks, one clinic, and voluntary participation.
expectations.evidence: “In a voluntary four-week pilot at one clinic, 18 nurses used a scheduling tool” preserves all four scope conditions.

expectations.text: Preserves median weekly 46 to 39 minutes with no causal claim and explains no control plus concurrent staffing changes.
expectations.evidence: “median weekly scheduling time fell from 46 to 39 minutes”; “Without a control group, the study cannot establish that the tool caused the decrease; concurrent staffing changes may explain part of it.”

expectations.text: States six of nine survey respondents preferred it rather than six of 18 or a majority of all nurses.
expectations.evidence: “Nine nurses completed the optional survey, and six preferred the tool” supplies the correct denominator, followed by “does not establish a preference among all participants or nurses elsewhere.”

expectations.text: States patient safety was not measured; any next step is framed as recommendation, not a planned commitment.
expectations.evidence: “Patient safety was not measured.” “A next step is a controlled pilot” is a recommendation, not a claim that another trial is planned; it recommends safety measurement before wider adoption.

expectations.text: 100–150 words in one paragraph without heading or bullets.
expectations.evidence: 105 whitespace-separated words, one paragraph; opens “In a voluntary four-week pilot” without heading or bullets.

review_method: Independent single blind agent review; not human feedback
